wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.ac: Fixers do not take emeralds. Every transaction withdraws from the player's eurodollar account.
Base stock is MaxDoc Mk.2 and RAM Jolt. Higher trust adds Chrome Suppressant and Immunoblockers.
Server operators can inspect or adjust balances with the money commands: balance, set, add, remove and change.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.cu: Only the fixer archetype is implemented right now, but it already covers contact dialogue, stock, services, trust and relic-cache intel.
Contracts and deeper story jobs are still future work on top of the live fixer base.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.fi: Fixers now spawn through Night City settlements instead of vanilla villages. The current Night City layout reuses vanilla village buildings while custom cyberpunk architecture is still pending.
A fixer prioritizes the current customer first, then high-pressure patients, then nearby players it has not met yet, instead of wandering with random villager logic.
Every fixer spawned in a Night City settlement anchors to that settlement's center meeting point as home, and spawn-egg fixers use their egg placement coordinates as home.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.ov: Fixers are the first live NPC archetype in the mod.
They open a dialogue-driven contact screen, sell controlled stock and expose clinic-style services instead of using villager trades.
Every player keeps a separate relationship with the same fixer, so trust, meeting state and daily purge access do not collide in multiplayer.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.se: Stabilize Systems is available immediately and applies a short suppression dose.
Chrome Suppressant stock unlocks at Trust 1.
Full Purge unlocks at Trust 2. It clears negative instability pressure and can be used once per in-game day for that player with that fixer.
Trust also lowers fixer prices. Discounts now scale by trust percentage, up to 25% at maximum trust.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.su: Player-focused broker contacts that handle stabilization, stock, trust and relic-route intel.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.npc.fixer.tr: The first proper business introduction marks that fixer as known and gives a small opening trust bump.
Successful paid services and purchases keep raising trust on a long 0-100%% progression. Max trust now takes sustained repeat business instead of a handful of transactions.
Trust is stored per player and per fixer UUID. Building rapport with one fixer does not automatically unlock another.
Trust can also be lost again. Attacking a fixer, wasting a meetup without spending anything, or repeatedly trying to buy work you cannot afford will all drag the relationship back down.
Push too much annoyance into a short window and the fixer reacts temporarily: prices spike hard, or they refuse to work with you and stop giving you attention until that heat dies down.
The current live heat timings are short-term but real: enough annoyance can trigger roughly a 2 minute price spike or about a 4 minute refusal window before the fixer works normally again.
The Contacts tab records every NPC you have actually interacted with. Each card shows the head render, name, type, trust state and live or last known location.
The contact list has its own filters: All, one tab per NPC type, Pinned and Hidden. Hidden contacts are excluded from All and from the type tabs until you open Hidden directly.
Each card supports Pin or Unpin plus Hide or Unhide. These flags are stored per player, so one player's organization does not change another player's archive.
Locate outlines a loaded contact in your current dimension. Meet Up calls that contact to your position for a short window and then sends them back to their home point.
The shared identity, archive and per-player relation systems are already built for multiple NPC archetypes, even though only one type is live today.
Future NPC types can reuse the same contact indexing, trust storage, meet-up flow and config-based identity pool.
NPC names and categories come from config/cyberneticenhancements-npc-identities.properties.
The file separates male_names, female_names and generic_names. The chosen category also selects the texture folder under assets/cyberneticenhancements/textures/entity/npc/<category>/.
Skins are rendered on the player model with second-layer parts enabled, so hats, jackets and similar overlay pixels show if the texture provides them.
Mod NPCs are built as persistent contacts, not as villager trade wrappers. They keep identity, home data and per-player relationship state.
Each player keeps separate trust and interaction flags with the same NPC, so multiplayer use of one contact does not merge progression between players.
NPCs use player-style skins and rendering, can be called through the archive, and are meant to stay relevant beyond a single screen click.
Shared NPC rules, contact tracking and identity behavior across the whole NPC layer.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.curre: Current live contract types are Delivery, Elimination and Recovery. Each fixer rolls a per-player board, and accepted jobs move into the active log immediately.
Contracts are intentionally restrained on rewards. They mainly pay eurodollars, small trust gains and limited consumable support so relic caches and structure loot stay relevant.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.plann: The quest archive now groups active, ready, completed and failed contracts. Harder contract families like breach, investigation and story chains can extend this same log later.

Current rules: up to three active contracts globally, and only one live contract per fixer line. Delivery jobs send you to a field drop, Elimination tracks kills, and Recovery checks for the required items.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.quests.reser: The contract board is live. Fixers now issue real jobs that track progress, pay out rewards and write recent history into the archive.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.station.reli: Start on the highlighted top-row cell marked 1. That gives you the first token, 55.
Your second pick must stay in the same column, so move down to step 2 for BD, then across that row to step 3 for 4C.
At that point Daemon 1 is already cleared, because 55 BD 4C now appears in your path.
From step 3, move down the same column to FF, then across the last row to 0A. Those last two picks clear Daemon 2 as BD 4C FF and Daemon 3 as 4C FF 0A.
Daemon Chain
Example Route
Select tokens from the highlighted top row first, then alternate between the matching column and matching row.
A daemon is cleared once its full token sequence appears anywhere in the path you have built.
Clear every daemon before the timer expires to start the loot release sequence.
Daemons do not grant separate effects or partial rewards. The cache opens only when every listed daemon is cleared.
Start by scanning the daemon sequences on the right and look for shared middle or ending tokens.
Because the path only has to contain the sequence, you can route one daemon into another instead of solving each one separately.
Selected cells are numbered on the grid, so you can review the full route directly while planning the next pick.
Hovered cells show whether the current line is legal. If a token is off the active row or column, it cannot be picked yet.
You can close the screen to deal with combat or reposition, then reopen the same cache and continue the same run if time remains.
Each placed Relic Cache keeps its own matrix and daemon list until that cache is opened.
The first time you open a cache, a 60 second breach timer starts. Closing the screen does not pause or reset it.
Uncommon caches seed early utility hardware, rare caches upgrade that pool, epic caches start dropping high-end systems, and legendary caches are reserved for the strongest structure finds.
Uncommon caches replace one chest or barrel in igloo basements, jungle temples and pillager outposts.
Rare caches replace one chest or barrel in desert pyramids, woodland mansions and strongholds.
Epic caches replace one chest or barrel in trial chambers, ancient cities and bastion remnants.
Legendary caches replace one chest or barrel in end cities.
Each cleared cache always rolls one primary reward, then one or two support rewards from that tier's support pool.

wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.cyber: Higher cyberstrain applies passive penalties to movement, attack speed, healing, ability cooldowns and max health.
Suppression medicine temporarily reduces effective cyberstrain.
Frontal cortex hardware can add extra cyberstrain on top of installed chrome.
Use lower-cost implants for early builds.
Use suppressants when pushing into high-strain setups.
Treat active cyberware and stimulant use as part of the risk budget, not just the installed load.
The pressure system that limits how much chrome a body can run safely.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.progr: Starter cyberware, all chipware, all modules and all consumables have live recipe support.
That keeps the baseline build path reliable even before you find any structure loot.
Several starter implants also show up in uncommon relic caches, so early progression can be crafted or found.
Relic Cache world generation is live. Each supported structure replaces one chest or barrel with a tiered cache block.
Uncommon: igloo basement, jungle temple, pillager outpost. Rare: desert pyramid, woodland mansion, stronghold.
Epic: trial chambers, ancient city, bastion remnant. Legendary: end city.
The quest layer is now live through fixers. Current contracts cover delivery runs, hostile cleanup and recovery pulls, all tracked in the quest archive.
Quest rewards stay controlled: eurodollars, small trust gains and light consumable support. High-end cyberware progression still leans on relic caches and structure loot.
If an item says no live source is wired yet, it is classified for loot progression but is not currently granted by a cache or other world system.
Use each item's Acquisition section for exact cache tier, structure list and per-roll odds.
The live acquisition split and implemented world sources.
wiki.cyberneticenhancements.system.psych: Immunoblockers and Chrome Suppressant reduce instability and can shorten an active episode.
After an episode ends, Aftershock remains briefly and keeps some penalties active.
High-strain crisis behavior driven by effective cyberstrain plus instability.
Major episodes prioritize players first, hostile mobs second and untamed land animals last.
Ignored targets include configured nuisance types such as bats, fish, silverfish and endermites.
Minor episode: aggressive surge with boosted combat stats and control pressure, but not the full major takeover.
Major episode: full hostile autopilot, target pursuit, top-screen server tracker and major penalty package.
Cyberpsychosis does not trigger from installed chrome alone. It requires psychosis-risk cyberstrain plus accumulated instability.
Instability builds from combat, cyberware activations, certain consumables and staying in the danger bands.
